hedges.reason: This is the only candidate that carries the energy leg of my hedge thesis. The list has no Ukraine bonds, European defense stocks, ruble or Brent-spread instruments. A Trump-Putin summit before June 30 would most likely be staged to sign or announce a Ukraine ceasefire framework. Markets would then price in phased relief on Russian oil sanctions, a narrower Urals discount and less risk to Black Sea and refinery infrastructure, and that would pull front-month WTI down. The link is loose, because crude also moves on Iran tension (see E63), OPEC+ policy and US demand. That is why I choose only the mild tier.

claims.reason: The same mechanism links the two. The worlds where Trump and Putin do meet are the worlds where a settlement is concrete enough to justify a leaders' summit. In those worlds the Russia war-risk premium comes out of oil, and a path to sanctions relief adds expected Russian supply. Together these make a mild downside touch in front-month WTI likely before the end of June. I am only moderately confident in this claim, because an Iran escalation or an OPEC+ cut could offset it.
